full_parsed_json.title: Large-uniformity conjecture for hypergraphs without regular subgraphs
full_parsed_json.statement:
For a positive integer $r$, let $k_r$ and $n_k$ be thresholds, and let $H$ be an $n$-vertex $k$-uniform hypergraph. A **full $k$-star** is the family of all $k$-edges containing a fixed vertex. **Large-uniformity regular-subgraph conjecture.** For every $r$, there exist $k_r$ and $n_k$ such that, whenever $k>k_r$, $n>n_k$, and $r\mid k$, every $k$-uniform hypergraph $H$ with no $r$-regular subgraphs satisfies

$$
|H|\leq {{n-1}\choose{k-1}},
$$

and equality holds if and only if $H$ is a full $k$-star. This proposes the full star as the extremal example beyond the range proved in the main theorem; the source gives no resolution status.

full_parsed_json.title: The Galton–Watson conjecture for degree-weighted CMP
full_parsed_json.statement:
Let $\alpha\geq 1$, and let $G$ be a Galton–Watson tree with reproduction law $B$ satisfying

$$
\mathbf{E}[\exp(cB^{\alpha})]<\infty
$$

for every $c>0$. **Galton–Watson degree-weighted CMP conjecture.** Degree-weighted CMP on $G$ with expansion exponent $\alpha$ has a non-trivial phase transition, meaning that its critical parameter satisfies $0<p_c<1$. full_parsed_json.title: Residue-class unimodality conjecture for rational Catalan polynomials
full_parsed_json.statement:
Let $a<b$ be relatively prime, and write

$$
\mathbf{Cat}_{a,b}(q)=\sum_j c_jq^j.
$$

For each residue class $r$ with $0\leq r<a$, consider the coefficient sequence $(c_{ak+r})_k$ indexed by the integers $k$ for which these coefficients occur.

**Residue-class unimodality conjecture.** For every residue class $r$, $0\leq r<a$, the coefficients of $q^{ak+r}$ in $\mathbf{Cat}_{a,b}(q)$ are unimodal. The conjecture refines ordinary unimodality, which the source notes does not hold for the coefficients of $\mathbf{Cat}_{a,b}(q)$ in general. It is motivated by the shifted-coset formula above, but no resolution is supplied.

full_parsed_json.title: The prime-torsion conjecture for poset Lie algebra homology
full_parsed_json.statement: Let $\preceq$ be the poset defining the poset Lie algebra $\frak{gl}_n^\preceq$, and let $H_\ast(\frak{gl}_n^\preceq;\mathbb{Z})$ denote its homology with integer coefficients. For a prime $p$, say that the homology contains $p$-torsion if some homology group has an element of order divisible by $p$. **Prime-torsion conjecture.** If $H_\ast(\frak{gl}_n^\preceq;\mathbb{Z})$ contains $p$-torsion, then it contains $p'$-torsion for every prime $p'<p$. full_parsed_json.statement:

full_parsed_json.title: Shareshian–Wachs generalized q-Eulerian q-unimodality conjecture
full_parsed_json.statement:
For $\sigma\in{\mathfrak S}_n$, define

$$
{\rm inv}_{<r}(\sigma)=\left|\{(i,j):i<j,\ 0<\sigma(i)-\sigma(j)<r\}\right|,
$$

and

$$
{\rm maj}_{\geq r}(\sigma)=\sum_{i:\,\sigma(i)-\sigma(i+1)\geq r}i.
$$

For $r\in[n]$, set

$$
A_n^{(r)}(q,t)=\sum_{\sigma\in{\mathfrak S}_n}q^{{\rm maj}_{\geq r}(\sigma)}t^{{\rm inv}_{<r}(\sigma)}.
$$

**Shareshian and Wachs's conjecture.** For all $r\in[n]$, the palindromic polynomial $A_n^{(r)}(q,t)$ is $q$-unimodal. This is presented as a consequence of the chromatic-quasisymmetric-function conjecture. The source records the related unimodality question for $A_n^{(r)}(1,t)$ as still open.

full_parsed_json.title: Virtual combinatorial R-matrix conjecture for KR crystals
full_parsed_json.statement:
Let $B^{r,s}$ and $B^{r',s'}$ be KR crystals of type $D_4^{(3)}$, and let the virtual combinatorial $R$-matrix be induced by restriction of the type $D_4^{(1)}$ combinatorial $R$-matrix through virtualization. **Virtual R-matrix conjecture.** The virtual $R$-matrix is well-defined on

$$
B^{r,s}\otimes B^{r',s'}.
$$

Well-definedness would extend the virtual $R$-matrix construction from the cases already understood in the paper to arbitrary pairs of KR crystal factors.

full_parsed_json.title: The fixed-size independent-set extremal conjecture
full_parsed_json.statement:
Let $G$ be a $d$-regular graph with $2ad$ vertices, and let $i_t(G)$ denote the number of independent sets of size $t$ in $G$. Recall that $aK_{d,d}$ is the disjoint union of $a$ copies of $K_{d,d}$. **Fixed-size independent-set conjecture.** For every $t$,

$$
i_t(G)\le i_t(aK_{d,d}).
$$

This asserts that the disjoint union of complete bipartite graphs, already extremal for the total number of independent sets, is extremal at every fixed size. The conjecture remains open, with partial bounds known.

full_parsed_json.title: Iterated difference-product growth conjecture
full_parsed_json.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{R}$ be a finite set, and for a positive integer $k$ write

$$
(A-A)^{(k)}=\underbrace{(A-A)\cdots(A-A)}_{k\text{ factors}}.
$$

Here $X\gg_{k,l}Y$ means that $X\geq c_{k,l}Y$ for a positive constant depending only on $k$ and $l$. **Iterated difference-product growth conjecture.** For every $l>0$ there exists $k>0$ such that, uniformly for all sets $A\subset\mathbb{R}$,

$$
|(A-A)^{(k)}|\gg_{k,l}|A|^l.
$$

This conjecture predicts arbitrarily large polynomial growth from sufficiently many iterated products of a difference set. The paper notes that even the case $l=3$ appears beyond the methods developed there; no resolution is supplied.

full_parsed_json.title: Small-product-set difference containment conjecture
full_parsed_json.statement:
Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}$ be a finite real set, and let $XX=\{xy:x,y\in X\}$. Let $A\subset\mathbb{R}$ be a set with difference set $A-A=\{a-a':a,a'\in A\}$. **Small-product-set difference containment conjecture.** For every $\epsilon>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that, for every real set $X$ satisfying

$$
|XX|\leq |X|^{1+\delta},
$$

if

$$
A-A\subset X,
$$

then

$$
|A|\ll_\delta |X|^\epsilon.
$$

This is presented as an alternative form of the iterated difference-product conjecture: a set with very small multiplicative doubling should not contain the difference set of a substantially larger set. The source gives no resolution.

full_parsed_json.title: Conjecture on random Kneser graph chromatic number
full_parsed_json.statement:
Let $KG_{n,k}$ be the Kneser graph on the $k$-element subsets of $[n]$, and let $KG_{n,k}(p)$ be its random subgraph obtained by retaining each edge independently with probability $p$. Write $\chi$ for chromatic number. **Random Kneser graph conjecture.** For every fixed $p>0$,

$$
\chi\bigl(KG_{n,k}(p)\bigr)\ge \chi\bigl(KG_{n,k}\bigr)-4
$$

whenever $k\gg\log n$. This conjecture proposes that, in the indicated range, passing to a random subgraph lowers the chromatic number by at most an additive constant; the supplied passage states that the corresponding question is open and gives no resolution of this conjecture.

Let $KG(n,k)_{s-\mathrm{stab}}$ be the induced subgraph of the Kneser graph $KG(n,k)$ on the $s$-stable $k$-subsets of $[n]$, where a subset $A$ is $s$-stable when $s\leq |i-j|\leq n-s$ for every pair of distinct elements $i,j\in A$. **Meunier's conjecture.** If $n,k,s$ are non-negative integers such that $n\geq sk$ and $s\geq 2$, then

$$
\chi\left(KG(n,k)_{s-\mathrm{stab}}\right)=n-s(k-1).
$$

This generalizes the chromatic-number formula for Schrijver graphs, which are the case $s=2$. The source presents the assertion as Meunier's conjecture; no resolution is given in the supplied text.

full_parsed_json.title: Aharoni–Howard conjecture on rainbow matchings
full_parsed_json.statement:
For a positive integer $n$, write $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $\binom{[n]}{k}$ be the family of $k$-subsets of $[n]$. Let $\mathcal F=\{F_1,\ldots,F_t\}$ be a family of subsets of $\binom{[n]}{k}$, and call a set of pairwise disjoint edges, one from each $F_i$, a **rainbow matching**. **Aharoni–Howard conjecture.** If

$$
e(F_i)>\max\left\{\binom{n}{k}-\binom{n-t+1}{k},\binom{kt-1}{k}\right\}
$$

for every $1\le i\le t$, then $\mathcal F$ admits a rainbow matching. This is the family version of the Erdős matching conjecture and seeks a sharp edge-density condition guaranteeing a rainbow matching; the source provides no evidence of resolution.
full_parsed_json.source_name: Hongliang Lu, Yan Wang and Xingxing Yu, “A better bound on the size of rainbow matchings”, arXiv:2004.12561 (2021).
full_parsed_json.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2016–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1611.01735](https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.01735).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.12561

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2020).

full_parsed_json.title: Frankl's binomial norm conjecture for intersecting-union families
full_parsed_json.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $2^{[n]}$ denote its power set, and let an **IU-family** be a family $\mathcal F\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ in which any two members intersect and no two members cover $[n]$. Define its **binomial norm** by

$$
\lVert\mathcal F\rVert_n=\sum_{F\in\mathcal F}\binom{n}{|F|}^{-1}.
$$

**Frankl's conjecture.** For every IU-family $\mathcal F\subseteq 2^{[n]}$,

$$
\lVert\mathcal F\rVert_n\leq \frac{n+1}{6}.
$$

Frankl's circle-method argument gives the weaker bound $\lVert\mathcal F\rVert_n\leq n/4$; the conjectured sharp constant remains unresolved.
full_parsed_json.source_name: Yongjiang Wu and Lihua Feng, “The binomial norm of intersecting-union families”, arXiv:2607.07564 (2026).
full_parsed_json.references:
**5 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2016–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2508.14334](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.14334), [arXiv:2409.19344](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19344), [arXiv:2106.05355](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.05355), [arXiv:1603.01215](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.01215).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.07564

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2026).

full_parsed_json.statement: Let $\mathsf{T}$ be the tree in Fig., and let $T$ be any nontrivial tree with root $r$. Define $G_1=T(r) \odot \mathsf{T}(4)$ and $G_2=T(r) \odot \mathsf{T}(7)$. **Smith normal form conjecture.** The matrices $tI-L_\mu(G_1)$ and $tI-L_\mu(G_2)$ should have the same Smith normal form over $\mathbb{Q}(\mu)[t]$. The claim extends the preceding proved result from paths and stars to arbitrary nontrivial rooted trees; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
